claims.text: Nanoscale as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type films and nanoribbons have enhanced internal strain because of their high surface-to-volume ratio.
These as-deposited films and nanoribbons contain a dense network of structural defects and abundant grain boundaries arising from nanoconfinement and patterning.
Internal strain, grain boundaries, and dislocations pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning inhibits the reversible cooperative magneto-structural phase transition associated with the magnetocaloric effect.
Defect-mediated pinning increases magnetic hysteresis in the as-deposited nanoscale material.
Defect-mediated pinning diminishes the peak magnetocaloric response under low applied magnetic fields.
As-deposited films and nanoribbons exhibit broadened, hysteretic magnetic transitions and a suppressed magnetocaloric effect.
A mild post-deposition thermal anneal will relax residual stress.
A mild post-deposition thermal anneal will reduce defect density.
Reducing strain and defect density by annealing will sharpen the magneto-structural transition.
Annealed samples will have lower hysteresis width than otherwise identical as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will have a higher peak magnetocaloric coefficient than otherwise identical as-deposited samples.
The predicted response applies near the alloy-specific magneto-structural transition temperature under applied fields below 50 mT.
Cycle frequencies below 10 Hz are intended to accommodate heat-transfer-rate limitations.
The magnitudes of hysteresis reduction and magnetocaloric enhancement depend on annealing parameters and nanoscale morphology.
